Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3063); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region:--Juda(-h, -s); Jude.
BiblicalUsage: Judas is the name of the traitor, and of other men who bore it faithfully. In Matthew 10:4 Simon the Canaanite and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him, are named among the twelve, in Acts 1:16 Peter says the scripture must needs have been fulfilled concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus, and in Acts 15:22 the church sends Judas Barsabbas with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the name carries both stories at once: one Judas sold the Lord for silver, and another Judas carried the letter of freedom to the Gentiles.
RelatedEvents: Jerusalem Council; Paul's Missionary Journeys; Jesus Sends Out the Twelve; The Choice of Matthias
